name: Médoc
blurb: Left Bank peninsula north of Bordeaux; gravel soils and Cabernet-led blends. Climate point is Pauillac (also stands in for Haut-Médoc / communal AOCs such as Margaux, Saint-Julien, Saint-Estèphe).

name: Graves
blurb: Gravelly Left Bank south of the city; historic source of both red Bordeaux blends and dry whites (Sauvignon Blanc–Sémillon).

name: Pessac-Léognan
blurb: Northern Graves AOC around the city suburbs; classified growths for reds and age-worthy dry whites (e.g. Haut-Brion, Domaine de Chevalier).

name: Sauternes / Barsac
blurb: Cirón–Garonne mist belt for noble-rot sweet wines; Barsac is the adjacent commune AOC with a similar style. Station: Sauternes village.

name: Saint-Émilion
blurb: Right Bank limestone plateau and côtes; Merlot-dominant blends with Cabernet Franc, plus satellites under related AOCs.

name: Pomerol
blurb: Small Right Bank plateau of clay and gravel; Merlot-led wines (often with Cabernet Franc), no official classification.

name: Entre-Deux-Mers
blurb: Wedge between Garonne and Dordogne; AOC name is mainly for dry whites, while reds often label as Bordeaux / Bordeaux Supérieur. Station: Créon.

name: Blaye / Bourg
blurb: Right-bank AOCs facing the Médoc across the Gironde; Côtes de Blaye and Côtes de Bourg reds (Merlot-led) plus some whites. Climate point: Blaye.
